objective.statement: Recognise quavers and semiquavers and compare them with crotchets.
successCriteria: I know a quaver lasts half a beat and a semiquaver a quarter of a beat.
I know two quavers fit in one crotchet beat, and four semiquavers fit in one beat.
I can add up groups of short and long notes.

explanation.text: Some notes are shorter than a beat. A quaver lasts half a crotchet beat, so two quavers fit into one beat. A quaver has a solid head, a stem and one flag.
A semiquaver is shorter still: a quarter of a beat, so four semiquavers fit into one beat. It has a solid head, a stem and two flags.

music.textAlternative: A crotchet, a quaver and a semiquaver labelled with their lengths in beats: 1, a half and a quarter.

explanation.caption: Crotchet: 1 beat. Quaver: ½ beat. Semiquaver: ¼ beat.

explanation.text: Each extra flag halves the length. One crotchet = two quavers = four semiquavers. And one minim = two crotchets = four quavers.
Say 'one-and' for two quavers in a beat, and 'one-e-and-a' for four semiquavers in a beat.

music.textAlternative: One crotchet, then two quavers, then four semiquavers. Each group fills one beat.

steps: Press Play all and tap the beat. The crotchet takes one tap.
The two quavers share the next beat: 'one-and'. Each is half a tap.
The four semiquavers share the third beat: 'one-e-and-a'.
Each of these three groups lasts exactly one beat, but they are made of shorter and shorter notes.
demonstration.textAlternative: A crotchet, two quavers and four semiquavers, each group lasting one beat. The shorter the notes, the more of them fit into a beat.

guided.prompt: Which single note lasts as long as all of these notes added together?

minim.reason: That note is twice as long as the notes added together. Add the beats first, then find the note with that many.

quaver.reason: That note is only half as long as the notes added together. Add the beats first, then find the note with that many.

hints: Add the beats first.
Work out how many crotchet beats the notes last altogether.
Then find the single note that lasts that long.

feedback.correct: Yes: you added the short notes to find one long note.

mistakes.halved-or-doubled: That value is twice (or half) as long. Count it in crotchet beats and compare.
mistakes.dot-misread: Remember: a dot adds half of the note's own value. Work out that half, then add it.
mistakes.note-rest-confusion: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.
mistakes.tie-dot-confusion: A tie joins two notes into one sound, so add both values together.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.
